newsitem.title: USA: MoneyGram Payment IPO to price in lower range.
newsitem.headline: MoneyGram Payment IPO to price in lower range.

text.p: The estimated price range on MoneyGram Payment Systems Inc's initial public offering has been revised to $10 to $12 per share from $15 to $17 per share, said underwriter Morgan Stanley on Tuesday.
The 14.46 million share IPO is tentatively set to make its debut on the big board next week under the symbol "MNE".

The lower range should make the money wire-transfer provider's issue more attractive, said analysts. "At this level, it will garner some serious players," said David Menlow, president of Springfield, N.J.-based IPO Financial Network Corp. He sees a five percent or more premium at the opening.

Analysts feel the lowering of the price range reflects an increasingly choosy IPO market. "The market's changed," said John Fitzgibbon, editor of the IPO Aftermarket. "Investors are not jumping on the IPO bandwagon".

Adding to this could be a possible stigma that has attached itself to MoneyGram because its IPO has been in the pipeline since January, and has been amended a few times. "There are cobwebs over the stock," said Menlow.

But the company has good growth potential, analysts said, despite some concerns about its long-term ability to compete with Western Union Financial Services Inc, which holds about 80 percent of the worldwide money wire services business.

"This is fundamentally a sound business", said Travis Farr, analyst at Greenwich, Conn.-based Renaissance Capital Corp. "Transaction volume is growing at around 20 percent a year, and the company has great margins."
Lakewood, Colo.- based MoneyGram accounted for about 16 percent of consumer money wire transfer transactions worldwide in 1995, according to its prospectus.

It is being spunoff from First Data Corp because of a consent decree signed with the Federal Trade Commission at the time of First Data's merger with First Financial Management Corp - the parent of Western Union.
First Data agreed to manage the MoneyGram unit as a separate operation independent of all First Data businesses, including Western Union.
MoneyGram reported revenues of $94.2 million in 1995, up from $71 million in 1994. ---Kamalakshi Mehta, New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610
